findings.title: Firecrawl response size-cap error mislabels transport failures as size refusals
findings.description: bytes_with_limit distinguishes Ok(None) (size-cap refusal) from Err(_). The pre-fix code folded both into 'firecrawl response exceeded N bytes', misattributing TCP resets to a size policy.
findings.trigger: Firecrawl backend resets the TCP connection while serving a within-cap response.
findings.suggested_fix: Split: pass Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> through ?, map only Ok(None) to size-cap message. The Err arm goes through AlephError::network with the original error text.

findings.title: Firecrawl test success never persists verified=true
findings.description: handle_test writes verified=true only when backends.get_mut(name) succeeds. Per Strategy V firecrawl never lands in fetch.backends (filtered at handle_update:252), so the write silently no-ops and the Panel always shows verified=false for firecrawl even after a successful test.
findings.trigger: Operator runs fetch_config.test with provider_type=firecrawl after a successful connection.
findings.suggested_fix: Add FetchConfigInternal::verified_shared: HashMap<String, bool>. handle_test writes to backends[name].verified when present, else to verified_shared[name]. synth_firecrawl_dto reads verified_shared.

findings.title: Magic number 60 duplicated across fetch providers, builtin crawl4ai, and web_fetch policy
findings.description: Three independent 60-second defaults: Crawl4aiFetchProvider::from_backend unwrap_or(60), Crawl4aiBackend::default_timeout() const fn → 60, WebFetchPolicy::default_crawl4ai_timeout() const fn → 60. Changing one leaves the others stale.
findings.trigger: Future change to crawl4ai default timeout in one location only.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-export a single pub(crate) const DEFAULT_CRAWL4AI_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 60; and reference that from all three sites.
findings.deferred_reason: Low-impact hygiene; three-call-site refactor outside the immediate review scope.

findings.title: Secret redaction gap: firecrawl serde_json parse error can echo upstream body containing api_key
findings.description: The send() funnel redacts the bearer token on reqwest failures and body excerpts; the JSON parse step is outside that funnel. A misbehaving firecrawl server echoing the auth header in a non-JSON body would land the api_key in the operator-facing error.
findings.trigger: Captive portal / debug page returns non-JSON containing the Authorization header.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply a redact_secret helper at parse time. Either expose search/providers/base.rs::redact via pub(crate) or duplicate the two-line helper.
findings.deferred_reason: Low-probability leak vector; existing redaction elsewhere covers the more likely paths.

notes: Module is in a deliberately reduced state (commit ae8cc6497 dropped the inert [fetch] provider chain). Post-DNS-pin reduction removed most prior wiring surface. Two P2s fixed (size-error fold; verified persistence for firecrawl). Two P3s deferred as hygiene.
